architecture:
### Architectural Anatomy of the Current Invariant vs. Proposed Reversal

1. Current Invariant Boundary:
- Origin Asset Serving: The service origin serves exactly ONE static raster asset across the entire product: `/assets/card.v1.png` (a 1200x630 PNG). It is committed to `packages/relic-viewer/public/card.v1.png` and served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- Shell Head Generation: In `packages/relic-server/src/app.ts:shell()`, `og:image` and `twitter:image` are hardcoded to `${serviceOrigin}/assets/card.v1.png`. The alt text is a constant string asserting an unrevealed key line and empty accession label.
- Metadata & Telemetry Concession: Across `docs/frame.md`, `docs/spec/service.md`, and `packages/relic-mcp/src/server.ts`, the product asserts that the server stores and learns NOTHING about relic content beyond: (1) coarse renderer class (one of 8 values), (2) publishing client name/version, (3) ciphertext length / approximate size, (4) publishing IP and timestamp, and (5) publisher-declared plaintext title (defaulting to filename). It repeatedly asserts: "Metadata, never content", "The server cannot read a byte", and "Nothing content-descriptive crosses to the server".
- The Reversal: Rendering an image *from* the document plaintext client-side and uploading it to the server in the clear reverses this invariant: the server will now receive, store, and serve a visual depiction of the decrypted content itself.

2. Locked Rules Implementation Must Still Obey:
- Zero Minting on Metadata / Image Fetches: Fetching `/{id}` or the cover image MUST NOT execute a mint, increment `mintsUsed`, consume download cap, or write to `mint_log`. Unfurls are frequent and automated by chat bots.
- Caching & Content Addressing: Cover rasters must carry an immutable public cache policy (e.g., versioned or content-hashed URL) to prevent origin egress storms, bounded by crawler cache windows.
- Indexing Prevention: Responses must preserve `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Fallback on Tombstone, Expiry, or Store Failure: When a relic is removed (tombstone), expired, unknown, malformed, or if store read throws, the shell MUST drop any stored title and cover image, falling back cleanly to the constant generic card (`A relic`, `card.v1.png`, and constant copy).
- Viewer DOM Isolation: The viewer bundle on the viewing origin must never read card metadata or cover URLs from the DOM to drive viewer routing or behavior (`card-metadata-guard.test.ts`).
- Service Worker Precache Exclusion: Cover images must never be precached by the PWA service worker shell precache.
